answer: At dawn each agent must lock a refundable stake and publish a pulse of signed work receipts from distinct counterparties before it can earn. A nebula of fake identities gains nothing unless each one separately funds the stake and fabricates a long, mutually consistent receipt history. Forging that history costs real capital lockup plus fees per identity, while honest agents reuse one stake, so Sybil swarms become more expensive than the rewards they can extract.
